title: Business Requirements Document — Hospital Management System

sections.title: 1. Executive Summary & Strategic Rationale
sections.body: The Hospital Management System (HMS) is designed to provide a centralized, secure, and scalable platform for managing comprehensive hospital operations. The strategic rationale for this system is to digitize and streamline critical workflows—including patient registration, clinical care, laboratory, pharmacy, and billing—thereby reducing administrative overhead, minimizing human error, and improving the overall patient experience. By implementing a unified system with role-based access control, the organization aims to ensure the integrity and confidentiality of sensitive medical data while maintaining high operational efficiency across all departments.

sections.title: 2. Business Objectives & Success Metrics
sections.body:
**Business Objectives:**
1. Centralize hospital operations to eliminate data silos between departments (e.g., clinical, pharmacy, billing).
2. Enhance patient engagement through a dedicated portal for viewing medical history, appointments, and billing.
3. Ensure strict compliance with healthcare data privacy standards (HIPAA, GDPR) and industry interoperability standards (HL7 FHIR, DICOM).
4. Improve operational efficiency by automating workflows from patient admission to discharge and billing.

**Success Metrics:**
- **System Availability:** Achieve high availability with an RTO < 1 hour and RPO < 5 minutes.
- **Security Compliance:** 100% adherence to PHI encryption standards (AES-256 at rest) and audit trail immutability.
- **Operational Efficiency:** Reduction in manual processing time for patient registration and billing.
- **User Adoption:** Successful onboarding of all defined roles (Admin, Doctor, Nurse, etc.) with role-based access enforcement.

sections.title: 3. Scope & Operational Boundaries (In/Out of Scope)
sections.body:
**In Scope:**
- **Core Modules:** Authentication, Patients, Appointments, EMR, Doctors, Nursing, Laboratory, Pharmacy, Billing, Inventory, Staff, Reports, Notifications, and Administration.
- **Workflows:** Complete end-to-end workflows for OPD/IPD management, including patient registration, appointment scheduling, consultation, diagnosis, laboratory/pharmacy processing, billing, and follow-up.
- **User Roles:** Admin, Doctor, Nurse, Receptionist, Pharmacist, Lab Technician, Accountant, and Patient.
- **Technical Infrastructure:** Responsive web UI, REST APIs, secure authentication (JWT/OAuth), and database integrity mechanisms.

**Out of Scope:**
- Hardware procurement and physical infrastructure setup (unless specified as cloud deployment).
- Integration with external third-party insurance providers (beyond basic insurance management features).
- Advanced AI-driven diagnostic tools (not mentioned in source).
- Mobile native applications (source specifies responsive web UI).

sections.title: 4. Key Stakeholders & Governance Personas
sections.body:
The system is designed to serve a multi-stakeholder environment with distinct governance and operational roles:

1. **Administrators:** Oversee system configuration, user management, and overall operational metrics.
2. **Doctors:** Manage patient records, diagnoses, prescriptions, and clinical notes via dedicated dashboards.
3. **Nurses:** Handle nursing notes, vital signs, and patient care coordination.
4. **Receptionists:** Manage patient registration, appointment scheduling, and queue management.
5. **Pharmacists:** Manage medicine inventory, prescriptions, and pharmacy operations.
6. **Lab Technicians:** Process laboratory test requests and generate reports.
7. **Accountants:** Manage billing, payments, invoices, receipts, and hospital expenses.
8. **Patients:** Access personal medical history, appointments, prescriptions, reports, and bills via a patient portal.

sections.title: 5. Business Requirements Specification Matrix
table: Implement secure authentication and authorization for Admin, Doctor, Nurse, Receptionist, Pharmacist, Lab Technician, Accountant, and Patient roles.
Users can only access modules and data relevant to their role. Unauthorized access attempts are logged and denied.
Enable creation and management of patient profiles including demographics, medical history, and allergies.
Patient profiles are created successfully with all required fields validated. Data is encrypted at rest.
Provide tools for scheduling appointments, managing doctor availability, and handling patient queues.
Appointments can be booked, rescheduled, and cancelled. Queue status is updated in real-time.
Store and manage diagnosis, prescriptions, treatment history, vital signs, and nursing notes.
EMR data is accessible to authorized clinical staff. Audit logs record all access and modifications.
Manage lab test requests/reports and pharmacy prescriptions/medicine inventory.
Lab reports are linked to patient records. Pharmacy inventory levels are updated upon dispensing.
Handle billing, payments, insurance claims, invoices, and receipts.
Invoices are generated accurately based on services rendered. Payment status is updated in real-time.
Allow patients to view appointments, prescriptions, reports, bills, and medical history.
Patients can securely log in and view their personal data. Data is filtered to show only patient-specific information.
Implement comprehensive audit logs, data validation, and security measures including HTTPS and password encryption.
All critical actions are logged. System enforces HTTPS and AES-256 encryption for PHI.
Ensure regular backups and disaster recovery capabilities.
System meets RTO < 1h and RPO < 5min benchmarks. Backup integrity is verified regularly.

sections.title: 6. Assumptions & Operational Constraints
sections.body:
**Assumptions:**
1. The system will be deployed in a cloud or on-premise environment as per organizational preference.
2. All users will have access to the internet and compatible web browsers for the responsive UI.
3. Data migration from legacy systems (if any) will be handled separately and is not part of the core development scope.

**Operational Constraints:**
1. **Compliance:** The system must strictly adhere to HIPAA and GDPR regulations for patient data privacy.
2. **Interoperability:** The system should support HL7 FHIR and DICOM standards for medical data exchange.
3. **Performance:** API responses must be fast to ensure a smooth user experience, especially in high-traffic scenarios.
4. **Scalability:** The architecture must support horizontal scaling to handle increasing patient volumes and data loads.

sections.title: 7. Risk & Compliance Baseline
sections.body:
**Compliance Baseline:**
- **HIPAA:** Ensure PHI encryption at rest (AES-256) and in transit (HTTPS). Implement audit trail immutability to track access to sensitive data.
- **GDPR:** Ensure data minimization, right to erasure, and consent management for EU patients.
- **HL7 FHIR/DICOM:** Ensure data formats are compatible with standard healthcare interoperability protocols.

**Risk Mitigation:**
- **Data Breach:** Mitigated by robust encryption, role-based access control, and regular security audits.
- **System Downtime:** Mitigated by high-availability architecture, regular backups, and disaster recovery plans meeting RTO < 1h and RPO < 5min.
- **Non-Compliance:** Mitigated by continuous compliance monitoring and automated audit logging.

Hospital Management System 
A Hospital Management System (HMS)  should provide a centralized platform for 
managing hospital operations, patient information, medical records, appointments, doctors, 
nurses, staff, billing, pharmacy, laboratory, and inventory. The system should support  role-
based access  for Admin, Doctor, Nurse, Receptionist, Pharmacist, Lab Technician, 
Accountant, and Patient. Core requirements should include patient registration and profile 
management, appointment scheduling and queue management, doctor availability, O PD/IPD 
management, admission/discharge/transfer, electronic medical records, diagnosis, 
prescriptions, treatment history, allergies, vital signs, nursing notes, laboratory test requests 
and reports, pharmacy prescriptions and medicine inventory, bed/ward m anagement, billing 
and payments, insurance management, invoices and receipts, hospital expenses, staff 
management, and inventory/procurement. Patients should be able to view appointments, 
prescriptions, reports, bills, and medical history through a portal,  while doctors should have 
dashboards for appointments, patient records, diagnosis, prescriptions, and clinical notes. 
The system should also provide  dashboards, notifications, search/filtering, reports, audit 
logs, data validation, backup/recovery, security, and role -based authorization . 
Functional requirements should cover complete workflows such as  patient registration → 
appointment → consultation → diagnosis → laboratory/pharmacy → billing → follow -
up, and admission → bed allocation → treatment → investigations → discharge → final 
billing. Non -functional requirements should include responsive web UI, scalability, high 
availability, fast API responses , secure authentication, password encryption, session 
management, HTTPS, database integrity, auditability, privacy of medical information, error 
handling, logging, and regular backups. A suitable architecture can use  React/Next.js for 
frontend, FastAPI/Node.js/Spring Boot for backend, PostgreSQL/MySQL for database, 
REST APIs, JWT/OAuth-based authentication, Redis for caching/queues, and cloud or 
on-premise deployment , with separate modules for  Authentication, Patients, 
Appointments, EMR, Doctors, Nursing, L aboratory, Pharmacy, Billing, Inventory, 
Staff, Reports, Notifications, and Administration.
